# Compression helpers

<!-- status autogenerated section -->
<!-- end autogenerated section -->

This experimental package provides reusable compression writers and
decompression readers. Create a writer or reader once and reuse it across
operations to benefit from the internal pools. Instances returned by the
factories can be shared across goroutines; callers must coordinate access to
their input and output streams.

The factories support gzip, zlib, raw DEFLATE, LZ4, Snappy, and Zstandard.
An empty compression type or `none` returns `Nop`, which copies bytes without
compression. The writer factory also accepts `x-snappy-framed` as a Snappy alias.

## Usage

```go
params := configcompression.CompressionParams{
    Level: configcompression.DefaultCompressionLevel,
}

writer, err := xcompression.NewWriterFactory().NewWriter(configcompression.TypeGzip, params)
if err != nil {
    return err
}
reader, err := xcompression.NewReaderFactory().NewReader(configcompression.TypeGzip, params)
if err != nil {
    return err
}

var compressed bytes.Buffer
if _, err := writer.CompressBytes(&compressed, payload); err != nil {
    return err
}
_, err = reader.DecompressBytes(dst, compressed.Bytes())
return err
```

Import this package as
`github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/pkg/xcompression`
and compression configuration as
`go.opentelemetry.io/collector/config/configcompression`.
`Compress` and `Decompress` also accept input streams through `io.Reader`.
The returned byte counts describe the uncompressed data. Caller-provided
streams remain open.

## Leasing

`NewReadLeaser` and `NewWriteLeaser` provide direct access to pooled readers and
writers through callbacks. Inside the callback, reset the supplied value to the
desired source or destination and close it when finished. Closing a writer
finishes its compressed stream. Use deferred cleanup so closing also runs on
errors and panics. The lease method returns the callback's error
and returns the value to the pool, including when the callback panics.

The supplied value is valid **only during the callback**. Do not store it for
later use or let a goroutine use it after the callback returns. Another operation
may immediately reuse it; accessing it afterward can cause data races and
corrupt data. The empty compression type and `none` do not support leasing.

## Benchmarks

Run from this directory:

```sh
go test -run '^$' -bench 'Benchmark(CompressWriter|DecompressReader)PoolDefaultCompressionLevel' -benchmem ./...
```

The benchmarks compare reusing a pool with creating a new pool for each
operation. The latter includes factory lookup, pool construction, and codec
initialization. They use a repetitive 46,080-byte payload and discard output;
results depend on the codec, payload, and machine.
